title: Canonical scalar-extension isomorphism of finite affine Cech complexes
statement: Let R and S be commutative rings with an R-algebra structure on S, f:X -> Spec R separated, U a finite family of affine opens (not necessarily covering X), and M a quasi-coherent module. Use the scheme, module, pullback, and coefficient constructions of [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [pqf-def-coherent], [pqf-def-cohomology], [def-pc-base-change], [def-pc-flat-cohomology-comparison], [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Define POver(f,M) by restricting the global-functions presheaf of M along R -> Gamma(X,top), and COver(f,U,M) as the ordered Cech complex in ModuleCat R. Let U_S be the inverse-image family on X_S and M_S the module pullback. There exists a chain map c:(extendScalars R S)(COver(f,U,M)) -> COver(f_S,U_S,M_S) which is an isomorphism and has the canonical coordinate formula: at each tuple intersection c(b tensor x) equals the restriction of the adjunction-unit pullback of the coordinate of x, multiplied by the image of b under S -> Gamma(X_S,top) -> Gamma(X_S,tuple intersection). Flatness is not assumed. The predicate IsCechBaseChange specifies this coordinate formula alone, without requiring invertibility.

proof.text: Choose degreewise canonical isomorphisms and their pure-tensor coordinate formulas by exists_cechBaseChange_term_isos; supply the finite-intersection inverse-image inclusion using baseChangeCover_intersection_le.

Apply cechBaseChange_components_comm to the hom maps of these isomorphisms and their coordinate equation. CochainComplex.ofHom assembles them into a chain map. Its formula is exactly the canonical-coordinate predicate. Every component is an isomorphism, so HomologicalComplex.Hom.isIso_of_components proves the chain map invertible.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_cechBaseChange_iso (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of R)) [IsSeparated f]
    [Finite ι] (U : ι → X.Opens) (hU : ∀ i, IsAffineOpen (U i))
    (M : X.Modules) [M.IsQuasicoherent] :
    ∃ c : tensorCech (S := S) f U M ⟶
      cechOver (baseChangeSnd (S := S) f) (baseChangeCover (S := S) f U)
        (baseChangedModule (S := S) f M), IsCechBaseChange f U M c ∧ IsIso c
